summary: An excerpt from the opening of Thomas Hoover's novel Life Blood, narrated by Morgan Smyth James, a 38-year-old single New York filmmaker driving to a location shoot for her first feature film, Baby Love, about adoption. Reflecting on her life, she regrets not having the family she once planned, explaining that at 20 she turned down two men and later adopted a defense habit of boxing up heartbreak. The excerpt ends as she begins to notice something changing three years back.
one_line: Opening excerpt of Thomas Hoover's novel Life Blood, following filmmaker Morgan Smyth James on the day her first feature wraps.
key_facts: Life Blood is a novel by Thomas Hoover, and this note is part 1 of its Book 3.
The story is set in New York, New York, on a blissful spring morning, cloudless and blue.
The narrator, Morgan Smyth James, is driving a high-mileage Toyota down Seventh Avenue.
She is headed for a location shoot meant to wrap principal photography for her first feature film, Baby Love.
Baby Love is about the pain and joy of adoption.
Morgan Smyth James is thirty-eight, single, and strives to be eternally optimistic.
Her name is after two grandmothers.
Morgan is missing a man named Steve terribly on that morning.
Eighteen years earlier, just out of college, Morgan turned down two really nice guys.
Morgan feared getting "trapped" into motherhood more than anything when she was in her twenties.
At NYU film school she met a director named Jason, who dumped her for his undergraduate sweetheart.
After Jason's betrayal, Morgan developed a fallback strategy: she put all heartbreak in a special box, nailed down the lid, and acted as though it wasn't there.
Morgan admits that people accuse her of living in selective denial and that they are right.
Morgan decided to focus her life on learning to make movies and let the family part play out naturally.
The excerpt ends with Morgan having started lingering, three years before the present, in a way she had not noticed.
